findings.finding: F1 — The 'look again' that starts a held child has no owner, no scan and no surface today: record.Waiting carries roots only, and Engine.gateOpened is reached only from enterChild and from advanceAdmittedTree when the design gate opens.
findings.answer: Plan task T4 adds the exported Engine.StartUnblockedChildren and calls it from Admission.promoteHolds after the root loop, passing the issues slice and mirror rows that call already holds. Every fact, the controller tick (admit.go:103-110), the hold release (admit.go:963, which calls promoteHolds directly) and the boot Reconcile (admit.go:328) reach promoteHolds, so each is a look. T11 pins it with a workflow test asserting phase.Planning, the IssueBranch row and the planner start inside the blocker's own fact transaction.

findings.finding: F2 — The mirror write has no safe seam: in admit.Admission (second) the engine judges a child against a stale row in the same transaction; in workflow.Engine four early returns skip it, one of them engine.go:186-188, the blocked-by-only edit the feature exists for; and settleObserved sets handlers = nil for an Observed fact whose issue is already recorded (facts.go:691-697).
findings.answer: Decision D1: a blockers.Mirror handler of its own, placed first in the chain at daemon/workflow.go:268-271, so both handlers and every fact kind see the row. The one path it does not see is the apply == false Observed fact; the plan states why nothing depends on it (release_children builds its held list from the Dispatch read releasableChild already makes) and that the next event, the periodic turn or boot repairs the row. T11 pins the order by behaviour with an intake test: a blocked-by-only issue.updated whose status did not change writes the row, and one ApplyFact for the blocker's close both admits the waiting root and starts the held child.

findings.finding: F3 — The mirror's rows, lifecycle and sequence fence are underspecified in four places: which issues get a row, when a row is removed, what the comparison is, and whether the boot read's own deferral applies.
findings.answer: Decisions D2, D3 and plan task T2 state all four: a row for every issue of the project the daemon observes, blockers empty or not; never removed, because Dispatch has no issue delete (routes_table.go:86-95) and moves no issue between projects; written only when the incoming sequence is strictly greater, the comparison record.Issue.LastDispatchSeq already uses at admit.go:289 and :481, expressed as an on-conflict guard in SQL, so a zero-seq synthetic fact (admit.go:1105-1112) writes nothing; and the boot write happens for a summary Reconcile defers to the consumer too, since the fence protects it. T11 pins each direction.

findings.finding: F4 — The periodic turn's re-read has no place to run, no bound and no failure rule; admission runs inside the fact transaction and does no I/O.
findings.answer: Decision D11 and plan task T6: the read runs in workflowRuntime.tickController before ApplyFact, in a short read transaction that collects the waiting set and its unfinished blocker keys; GetIssue per key while they number 25 or fewer, one whole-project ListIssues above that (the listing is a single unpaged request, client.go:40-70, and Dispatch caps an issue at 20 blockers, issue_parent.go:48-51); the rows ride on intake.ControllerTick{Observed}. A failed read logs at warn and the tick is applied anyway, because it is also the controller's daily-report wake and the only wake a tree on a refused claim gets.

findings.finding: F5 — record.Waiting has four callers and only two may learn the check; filtering inside it would make record.TreeLive false for a blocked root and turn its children into orphans admitted as roots of their own.
findings.answer: Decision D5: record.Waiting is left exactly as it is; the check goes in promoteHolds, as a third continue beside ErrCleanupReserved (:805-807) and ErrAuthorityHeld (:811-813) and before OpenTreeLifecycle (:804), and in slotFree's count only. T11 pins both consequences: a child of a blocked root is recorded as that child, and slotFree reports free when every root in the queue is blocked.

findings.finding: F6 — The contract bump names six artefacts and two strict wire shapes, and nobody has named the field.
findings.answer: Plan task T8 lists them: api.Admission gains blocked []{issue, blockedBy[]} with waiting left as roots only; WaveReleaseResponse gains started and held (decision D9); DaemonAPIVersion moves to 37 (main took 36 for INFRA-229 while the branch was open) with its ledger entry; legionAdmission and LegionWaveReleaseResponse in packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts; the recorded examples rewritten with go test ./internal/api/ -update and ./internal/projection/ -update; and legion.daemonApiVersion 37 in packages/pi-legion/package.json and packages/claude-envoy/package.json.

findings.finding: F7 — Every start path must be classified: three must learn the check and three must not, or one is missed in either direction.
findings.answer: Plan task T4 names all six. Learn it: Engine.enterChild (all three child doors funnel through it), Engine.advanceAdmittedTree, Admission.promoteHolds. Do not, and are named so nobody edits them: Admission.startMidPhaseMembers (already skips phase.Admitted because RoleFor is empty), Admission.reenterStrandedChildren (guarded on phase.Done), and the carry branches of readmit/consumeHandover, whose test is startedRun — which decision D6 also applies to a waiting root, so a candidate carrying a run is admitted whatever its links say.

findings.finding: F8 — The notice the spec relies on is not the notice the code sends: child-status cannot fire for a held child's start, because the child is already todo; what fires is phase-finished with phase admitted and an empty role.
findings.answer: Decision D7 as the architect ruled on 2026-10-25: a held child's start tells the tree's architect with the existing child-status notice, from a third producer of that kind (workflow/effects.go ChildUnblockedNotice), its reason naming the child, its root and what cleared the hold (the last blocker done, or the links taken off). The spec's words ('the notice it already receives when a child of its tree changes state') therefore hold as written, and specDepartures is empty.

findings.finding: F9 — The hand-over of a never-started child is narrow or broad, and the two change different sets of trees; the owner must confirm.
findings.answer: Decision D8 plans the narrow rule — hand over an admitted child only when its mirror row shows an unfinished blocker — because the spec's 'such a child' reads back to 'a child still waiting on blockers'; the architect confirmed the narrow reading on 2026-10-25.

findings.finding: F10 — Three acceptance lines no machine can decide as written: 'the only writes that follow are admission's own', 'reads the status table once per look', and 'the rule it encodes survives'.
findings.answer: The plan restates each as a check. The first is a daemon test admitting an unblocked root and a formerly blocked one and comparing them row for row — the same outbox payload kinds and the same issue-record and slot mutations. The second is 'at most one mirror query per promoteHolds call, whatever the number of blocked candidates', proven by a counting store in the workflow/stranded_test.go:42-60 style. The third re-points TestIssueEventIgnoresUnconsumedBlockedByFields at priority alone, renames it, and keeps its assertion that the decoded fact is unchanged.

findings.finding: F11 — Unsaid everywhere: what the check does when a blocker key has no mirror row, which a child created moments earlier can produce.
findings.answer: Decision D4: a blocker with no row counts as not done, so the child is held; the periodic turn and the boot listing bound how long. T11 pins it with an API test — a release naming a blocker the daemon has never observed holds the child and names that blocker in the answer.

findings.finding: F12 — The driven proof cannot run in a worker pod as the harness stands: turning Dispatch's events on needs a NATS server, testnats.URL can only start a testcontainer, and this pod has no Docker and may not submit a cluster workload (kubectl answers yes/no/no against the three the docs require).
findings.answer: The driven proof needs a NATS server the pod can reach without Docker. main now carries that door itself (packages/daemon/internal/testnats/nats.go:49-50, LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL and LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL), which the branch adopted at d7e29553 in place of its own; the container path stays for CI. plan.md v4 task G4 gives the local recipe on the issue's volume ($TMPDIR).

findings.finding: F13 — The docs bullet is missing the controller skill, whose tick row documents the payload, and the generated Claude plugin mirror, whose drift check fails.
findings.answer: Plan task T9 adds skills/legion-controller/SKILL.md:244 and :394 to the documentation task and requires bun scripts/build.ts in packages/claude-envoy, whose tests/legion-plugin-fresh.test.ts fails on drift.

findings.finding: F14 — Sourcing: the spec's claims about Dispatch hold, with one qualification — the cycle refusal is enforced at write time only and assertNoWaitPath gives up past parentDepthCap, so a pre-existing cycle costs a permanent wait rather than a loop.
findings.answer: Recorded so nobody adds cycle detection: the plan adds none, and the spec's own 'an issue nobody ever finishes' paragraph already covers the permanent wait, which decision D11's periodic re-read and plan task T8's reporting make visible to the operator and the controller.

findings.finding: G1 (generation 3) — Correcting only specDepartures and the F8 answer leaves plan.md v3's 'One stale record … not edited again' paragraph false and other plan.json answers stale against what was built: F6 says contract 35 to 36 (the code is 37), F9 says 'reported to the architect to confirm' (confirmed), F12 describes a testnats door the branch no longer builds, and plan.md names neither migration 0052 / TakenBack nor the links-off child-status start.
findings.answer: plan.md v4 adds 'Settled since this plan was first written' (contract 37, migration 0052 and record.Issue.TakenBack, main's testnats door, the links-off child-status start) and replaces the stale-record paragraph. This plan.json rewrites F6, F8, F9 and F12 and sets specDepartures to [] because with child-status the spec's acceptance words hold as written.
